summary:
Re-validated HEAD 32ce91a after the window-size rework (build 41) and the O-028 drive-row fix (build 42). The only changes since my last pass at 6fb88c8 are in the App (MainWindow.xaml/.cs, WindowReport.cs), the test hook and the window cases. Core and Core.Tests are byte-identical.

Checks against the project:
- Release build is clean.
- xUnit 181/181, Fitness 29/29, rules-parity AGREE, rules-harness CLEAN.
- WindowCases 26/26 (C-001..C-014, O-016, L-001..L-003, B-001..B-008). HookCases 2/2.

Contact with reality: I drove the published exe against the real C:\ drive, about 3.585M files and 664 unreadable folders. Each run used the project's own hook (watch, expand, MINSIZE, DRIVES=26). For sizes the hook cannot set, a throwaway startup hook in %TEMP% set the size, rendered the window's content to PNG and measured every row's location. It has been deleted.

The defect that failed my attempt 3 is gone. At the window's minimum of 560x620, a stopped C:\ scan with the unreadable folders open and 29 drive buttons gives:
- LargestFilesList 56 px, in view, 2 full rows.
- UnreadableList 41 px, 1 full row.
- TopLevelList 61 px, 1 full row.
- The outcome texts show 43 of 118 px; the rest is a scroll away.

Every other ending I drove also kept every list in view with at least one full row:
- Stopped, closed, at 560x620.
- Finished, opened, at 560x620 with 29 drives.
- Finished, closed, at the default 880x620.
- Finished, opened, at 880x620 with 29 drives.
- Stopped, opened, at 700x620.
- Stopped, opened, maximized (1936x1048): 12 full rows.

PickerPanel was 152.78 px with 3 and with 29 drive buttons, so O-028 holds on real data. Ranking took 30.0 to 36.2 ms on real C:\, under O-021's 100 ms. The top three rows match independent readings: docker_data.vhdx 55,430,873,088 B equals the report's largestFileOnDisk, pagefile.sys is 20.0 GB and hiberfil.sys 12.5 GB.

For the first time on this slice, the rendering was looked at, not just the report numbers. The 560x620 C:\ image shows every list drawn with its rows. A planted tree shows the lone-surrogate name drawn as 'a□b-lone-surrogate.bin' with no crash, and 'big-dot.' and 'big-space' drawn intact.

What does not hold as the design wrote it: design acceptance item (3), "each row shows the file's full path, never clipped". Since build 41, a location wraps to at most 3 lines and is then cut with an ellipsis, and the whole path is only in a hover tooltip. Because the end is cut, the file's own name is what disappears.
- A planted 408-character location is cut at both 880 and 560 px wide.
- On real C:\, 0 of the 100 locations are cut at the default width (the longest is 162 characters, 2 lines). At the 560 px minimum, 2 of 100 are cut (159 and 162 characters).

I do not grade this as a criterion failure. Criterion 7's own reason is that the returned path is exact, and that holds: EachPathIsTheFilesExactPath passes. The person's later rule, one full row in every list at any allowed size for any length of text, cannot be met while a row shows an unbounded path, so where the two conflict the person's rule wins. Nobody chose cutting the end, which hides the name, over keeping the name visible. That is left for a person in not_reached, as is the default 880x620 window showing only 2 of the 100 rows and scrolling part of the ending's detail.

Loop note: the outcome layout has been reworked five times, for O-024, O-025, O-027, the width rework and O-028. Each lap changed src, so it was progress, not the no-src loop. The earlier no-src loop was the 28 provider refusals (builds 9-36), which reflect already named.

I changed nothing in the tree. git status is the same as at the start.

not_reached: No person looked at the live window. I viewed in-process renders of its content, without window chrome, at 560x620, 880x620 and 880x900. Hover tooltips (the only place a cut-off location is shown whole), scrolling the outcome's texts, clicking the expander and dragging the window to a new size were not exercised by a person or by input.

A person's call on how a bounded row shows a long location. Build 41 cuts the end, which hides the file's name. Nobody chose that over keeping the name visible (e.g. cutting the folder part in the middle). On this C:\ that affects 0 of 100 rows at 880 px and 2 of 100 at 560 px; any path over about 300 characters is cut at the default width.

Whether the default experience is acceptable. At the default 880x620, which is also the minimum height, the list shows 2 of its 100 rows. On a system drive the ending's detail (the volume-coverage line and 'Read in') is partly a scroll away. This meets the person's one-full-row rule; nothing measured whether it is enough.
Non-100% DPI, larger text scaling, Windows 10, and displays whose work area is under 620 DIPs (e.g. 768 px tall at 125%), where the window's MinHeight cannot fit.
The on-disk sizes of pagefile.sys and hiberfil.sys: opening either fails unelevated with error 32, and no named elevated operation reads a file's allocation. Only logical sizes were compared.
A row-by-row check of all 100 real rows and a completeness walk at this HEAD. Core is unchanged since they passed (6fb88c8 and 658ed6a). The walk skipped OneDrive cloud-reparse folders.
An open-and-growing file identified as a real row; that shape rests on the spike.
The contents of the 664 unreadable folders on C:\, which the list cannot include.
Drives other than NTFS C:\ (exFAT/FAT removable media, a mapped SMB share) with the list shown. N-001..N-004 were not run.
